doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents, teachers' families, and his accordion-playing brother
summary: His parents were both New York teachers of Belarusian and Hungarian descent; he has an older brother who played accordion.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Francis. Her maiden name was Gatina – Hungarian, Alsace, a little German, and my father was a Liebman. They were from Belarus, White Russian Minsk, around

that area. My father was – a grandfather – I never met him. I think he died when I was very young – he was a butcher, upper East – East Harlem. My mother lived in Brooklyn. I think that’s where they were always, like Crown Heights, that area. They met through school, teaching, because they were both teachers.
So you’re a first generation American.
I would be second, right? No, I’m second generation, because I’m talking about the grandparents coming from the Old World. My parents were born here.
What did your father do for a living?

Teacher. That was the Board of Ed., New York school system, both my parents. Eventually my father, his last 10 years, 15 years, was an assistant principal in Brooklyn, Ditmas Junior High, and he was out in Rockaway. My mother was in Rockaway. My father was in Borough Park and then at Ditmas Junior High. My mother was in Bedford-Sty, because when I was a kid, I used to go – we had to go to the hospital. I would go spend the day with her. Then she ended up in Far Rockaway. The Board of Ed., until they retired.
My mother died in 2006 or ’7. My father died in ’86.
I have an older brother, five years older. I’m not sure where he is now. I think he’s in Las Vegas. We’re not in contact.
He played accordion, which I got to say, that’s what I first saw. But nothing more than that.
